topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the final lecture of the course and outlines the key learning objectives regarding cancer therapy.

topics.label: Conventional cancer therapies and drug resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine traditional local and systemic treatment modalities along with the resulting toxicities and cellular resistance mechanisms.

topics.label: Exploiting intrinsic cancer vulnerabilities and defects
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics focus on therapeutic strategies that exploit intrinsic biological vulnerabilities in cancer cells, such as signaling dependencies, checkpoint defects, and repair deficiencies.

topics.label: Kinase inhibitors, oncogene addiction, and resistance
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore small-molecule kinase inhibitors designed to exploit oncogene addiction, alongside the molecular mechanisms underlying acquired drug resistance.

topics.label: Antibody-based targeted therapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the design and clinical application of monoclonal antibodies to target tumor cell-surface proteins and deliver cytotoxic payloads.

topics.label: Cancer immunology and immunotherapies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics review the principles of natural anti-tumor immunity and the development of immunotherapies that reactivate or redirect immune responses against cancer.

topics.label: Challenges, historical progress, and future paradigms in cancer management
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics provide an overarching evaluation of clinical hurdles, historical survival improvements, and future directions in cancer treatment and trial design.
